::: {#thm-doubling-closed}
#### A formula for the double-minus-one sequence

Let $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ be the sequence with $a_0 = 2$ and $a_n = 2 a_{n-1} - 1$ for every integer $n \ge 1$
(@exm-doubling-sequence).
Then $a_n = 2^n + 1$ for every non-negative integer $n$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

We use induction (@def-proof-by-induction), following @rem-induction-template with $n_0 = 0$.
Let $P(n)$ be the equation $a_n = 2^n + 1$.

**Base case.**
$a_0 = 2 = 2^0 + 1$.

**Inductive step.**
Let $k \ge 0$ be an integer, and suppose $P(k)$: $a_k = 2^k + 1$.
The goal $P(k + 1)$ is $a_{k + 1} = 2^{k + 1} + 1$.
Since $k + 1 \ge 1$, the recursive rule gives $a_{k + 1}$, and

$$
\ba
a_{k + 1}
&= 2 a_k - 1
&& \text{(recursive rule)}
\\&= 2 \paren{2^k + 1} - 1
&& \text{(induction hypothesis)}
\\&= 2^{k + 1} + 2 - 1
\\&= 2^{k + 1} + 1.
\ea
$$

So $P(k + 1)$ holds, and by induction $a_n = 2^n + 1$ for every non-negative integer $n$.

:::

:::
